subject: SignalForge: dedicated pool runway + spike-hedge proposal
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex@signalforge.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@signalforge.com>
Date: 2027-05-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask + expected burst profile

Hi Hannah —

Thanks again for the deep dive last week. We ran the traffic sims on our end and wanted to share the expected production shape so we can lock on a Dedicated proposal. Key context:
- Primary model: open-variant, ~13B (production-intended, will choose quantized 4-bit in prod).
- Daily traffic: steady daytime window (09:00–21:00 PT) with two short spikes after product releases.
- Current beta metrics (weekly): average 12 req/sec, median tokens/request 180, 95th req/sec spikes up to 42 for short windows.

Questions:
1) Can you map those numbers to tokens/sec and give GPU sizing for a committed Dedicated pool with 20% headroom?
2) If we choose a 1-year reserved commitment, what burst policy would you recommend (and what does it cost to enable 2x burst for 10% of traffic)?
3) We'd like an SLO target of p95 latency <= 450ms for request end-to-end — can that be met with a quantized 13B on your Dedicated offering?

Thanks — attaching the CSV we used for the sim.

— Alex
Product Ops, SignalForge

Attachment: signalforge_beta_traffic.csv (CSV, 48KB)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Mercer <alex@signalforge.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Priya Rao <priya@signalforge.com>
Date: 2027-05-12T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask + expected burst profile

Alex — thanks for the data, this is exactly the right level of detail. I ran a quick mapping with Karthik and Ben; below is a concise first-pass sizing and recommendation. We'll follow up with an attachment that shows per-minute peak mapping.

Summary mapping (first-pass):
- Observed peak req/sec: 42 rps. Average tokens/request: 180 => peak tokens/sec = 42 * 180 = 7,560 tokens/sec.
- Recommended safety headroom: 1.5x for unmodeled bursts + cold-starts => target provisioned tokens/sec = 11,340 tps.
- Performance basis: quantized 13B (4-bit) on our Dedicated runtime yields ~5,600 tps per A100-equivalent GPU for interactive sequences (p95 token generation latency budget).
- GPUs required (provisioned): ceil(11,340 / 5,600) = 3 GPUs.
- Recommended committed pool: 4 GPUs to give operational breathing room (adds ~12% extra capacity beyond strict math for maintenance, KV cache warming, and multi-tenant overhead).

SLO fit:
- With the recommended 4-GPU pool and Redwood's prefix caching + request prioritization, we estimate p95 end-to-end ~350–420ms for the quantized 13B on typical prompt sizes (<= 250 tokens output). That meets your p95 <= 450ms target in normal conditions.
- If your traffic shifts to longer outputs or model size increases, latency will push up; we recommend a regression alert tied to a canonical prompt set so we can catch regression early.

Burst policy (short answer):
- Option A (burst credit pool): allow 2x burst for up to 10% of monthly tokens for an incremental fee; this maintains dedicated isolation but allows short spikes. Cost uplift estimate: ~+22% of committed spend for the burst envelope you described.
- Option B (fallback route): automatic routing to hosted instances for non-sensitive/less critical requests above committed capacity — lower cost, but implies data-plane differences (not suitable for regulated data).

Next steps:
1) I've attached a spreadsheet with the token-run mapping, minute-level peaks, and the 3/4 GPU scenarios.
2) Karthik will follow up with a short runbook for scaling/failover and a quantization checklist.
3) If that aligns, I'll draft a 1-year committed capacity quote (4 GPU pool + burst credit envelope) and send a DocuSign for approval.

Best,
Hannah
Director, Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference

Attachments: signalforge_stress_estimates.xlsx, dedicated_runbook_v1.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask + expected burst profile

Adding a technical run-through and quick sensitivity table. Alex — pasted the important bits inline for visibility.

Assumptions used:
- Model: quantized 13B, context length 2k (we benchmarked at 1024 and extrapolated).
- Measured throughput (internal bench): 5,600 tps/GPU @ p95 token-generation budget for short outputs; for longer outputs (>400 tokens) throughput degrades ~18%.
- Network + request orchestration overhead ~8% of token-time in our Dedicated topology.

Sensitivity table (tokens/sec requirement -> GPUs required before headroom):
- 6k tps -> 2 GPUs (theoretical 1.07x utilization)
- 9k tps -> 2 GPUs (but ~1.6x utilization if you want p95 margin; operationally we avoid >75% sustained util)
- 11,340 tps (your 1.5x headroom) -> 3 GPUs (75–95% util depending on output length)
- 15k tps -> 3–4 GPUs (recommend 4 for sustained spikes)

Operational recommendations:
- Start with 4 GPUs committed but configure autoscaling guardrails for horizontal scale to 5 GPUs for short windows (auto-burst) and auto-failover to hosted for anything beyond that.
- Enable prefix/KV caching for your high-frequency prompts (we can identify top-50 prefixes in your traffic sample). Caching reduces per-token compute and typically reduces effective tps requirement by ~20% for chat-style workloads.
- Quantization checklist: reproducible evals, calibration on representative inputs, and a safety/regression test harness (we can run this in our onboarding).

I'll attach a 1-page runbook snippet to the XLSX (already included in Hannah's attachment).

— Karthik
Principal Applied ML Engineer — Redwood Inference

— Priya

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask + expected burst profile

Priya/Alex — great questions, thanks. Action items and clarifications below so you have everything to hand: 

1) SLA & fallback behavior (short):
   - Burst credit envelope: enforced at the Dedicated control plane; when exhausted, traffic is either queued (shortly, up to 10s) or rejected depending on your routing policy. No cross-tenant data mixing; all processing remains in your VPC for Dedicated bursts.
   - Hosted overflow route: immediate spillover to Redwood-hosted clusters; faster to enable but data-in-transit to hosted control plane — we provide encryption in transit and at rest, and a SOC2-compatible boundary, but this is different from fully private Dedicated handling. Latency difference typically +80–150ms p95 depending on region.

2) Pricing delta (high-level estimate):
   - 4 GPU committed + burst credit envelope (2x for 10% monthly tokens): approx +22% on top of committed price.
   - 4 GPU committed + hosted overflow: approx +12% for overflow support (pay-as-you-go tokens beyond cap) but introduces the control-plane/data-plane tradeoff above.

3) Runbook excerpt (we will add the exact rollback checklist into the PDF runbook):
   - Alerting: p95 > 500ms for 5 consecutive 5-min windows triggers urgent page to SRE + account ops.
   - Immediate steps: (a) activate KV cache flush/warmup script, (b) add 1 GPU from autoscale guardrail (if allowed), (c) activate hosted overflow for non-PII traffic, (d) reduce max tokens/output on application side to short-circuit generation while we triage.
   - Post-incident: full traffic and prompt set replay for regression identification, and a quantization rollback to prior model weighting if error introduced by new quantization.

Next actions from Redwood:
- I'll send a formal quote (4 GPUs + burst envelope) and a DocuSign once you confirm preferred burst semantics (Dedicated-credit vs hosted overflow).
- HubSpot ticket: HS-29472 (I'll attach the quote there).

If you confirm you'd like Dedicated-credit burst, I'll issue the DocuSign today and we can target a 5/21 start for provisioning.

Thanks — Hannah
Director, Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference
